recipes.name: Quick Enchilada Sauce
ingredients_raw: 2 teaspoons chili powder, or more to taste

steps.text: Mix tomato sauce, tomato paste, beef broth, salt, oregano, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, and chili powder together in a saucepan until smooth.
Bring sauce to a boil, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Enchilada Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Just mix tomato sauce, tomato paste, and some spices together for a quick and very easy enchilada sauce you can whip up at a moment's notice.

review.reviewBody:
This is called "quick enchilada sauce" for a reason. It's very quick, and though one reviewer didn't like it because it tastes canned, but it sure is quick, compared to making the sauce from dried chiles, and unlike canned, you know what's in it because it's made at home. 
I have made this 3 times now. My husband loves it, my children love it, and I love that it's quick and easy.
Thank you, Tammy S, for sharing your recipe!

Good enchilada sauce when you haven't got any on hand. I doubled the spices and used 2 cups of chicken broth instead of beef. I also added 1/2 tsp. each of red pepper flakes, ground red cayenne pepper and minced garlic. After blending well, I simmered over a low heat for 20 minutes and cooled in the refrigerator overnight before using in any recipe. I think it gives the sauce's flavors a chance to blend together completely.

I made this sauce when I promised enchiladas for supper and didn't have my usual Old El Paso enchi sauce on hand. I'm not an adventurous cook, but I do okay, so I thought I'd give it a try since it was only supposed to take 10 minutes. I LOVED IT! And, I'm kind of picky, I wanted it to taste like The Old Passage city and it was spot on. I did tweak it a bit. I used the entire can of beef broth, so my recipe yielded 4 cups. I also doubled the cumin to 1/2 tsp and used more chili powder - 1 tbsp. I was so proud I took a picture, lol!

I didn't have a can of tomato sauce so I used a can of Rotel tomatoes, increased the onion powder and cumin to 1/2 tsp and put it in my blender with 3 cloves of garlic...the Rotel added some nice heat! Very good and EASY!
This recipe turns out great every time. I use ancho chilli powder instead of regular and let the sauce simmer for about an hour to get rid of the canned taste.

Ingredients are spot on! This is a great, quick recipe and, in spite of what one reviewer said, doesn't taste canned! My family like a thicker sauce, so I made a roux using the tomato sauce, doubled the spices (we also love spice!) and added the rest of ingredients as shown. Couldn't ask for a better quick and delicious enchilada sauce. Thanks so much - keep the great recipes coming!

It seemed a bit tomato heavy so I added less tomato paste. I also pretty much doubled the herbs and spices and I added some California chile powder, because I had it on hand. It tastes like good enchilada sauce to me. I used it on homemade mexican pizzas and everyone loved it!

Sorry...this is still like canned sauce. If you buy the mexican dried chiles (I use Anaheim or California ) soak them in hot water, then put in blender with your spices & beef broth then you have a quick, and DELICIOUS uncanned sauce.

THis was pretty easy and tasted good. I made it only because I didn't want to drive to the store when I didn't have enough sauce for my dinner. The only change I made was I used california chiles and toasted them and blended it with everything else because I had no chili powder.

I live in a small town, no enchilada sauce to be found, this was perfect as I had the ingredients on hand. I used chicken stock I had from roasting the chicken for the chicken enchiladas I was making so I used that instead of beef. I omitted the salt as well and I only needed a heaping tablespoon of paste to achieve the consistency I wanted.

Great recipe! I've been looking for the right enchilada sauce that I could control the ingredients due to allergies. This one is so easy and quick. I halved the amt of chili powder due to preference, and it was delicious. Thanks!!
This is a great , quick sauce ! I made it as written but added more spices according to my taste including paprika. It’s a keeper!
Absolutely delicious! Much better than pre-made in cans as you control the salt. Easy and fast to make so not an extra burden. This is my go-to enchilada sauce from now on.
Good sauce. I added a fresh serrano pepper for some heat

I love this recipe! I added green chiles and Smokey paprika to it suggested by a couple of reviewers.
We use it all the time. Love it. Do not like enchilada sauce with flour.

I didn't have cumin so I used paprika. It was so easy and delicious thank you!
